name: Meridian Field Office

text: A wall of weather traces, one long roll per station, forty stations.
Rain, pressure, wind, all of it going along in ordinary wiggles.
The coastal rolls are the flattest. Somebody has ringed them in pencil.
The Foundation's own account of itself, in a handsome frame.
Labs. Archaeology. Weather stations. Kin conservation. Ocean research.
Disaster relief. It is a good list. Most of it is true.
The public counter. Leaflets, in neat fans.
STORM SAFETY IN THE UPLANDS. REPORT A SICK KIN. GIVING TO THE FOUNDATION.
One leaflet has run out. The empty slot is labelled DEEP SURVEY.
A recruiting card. FIELD ASSISTANTS WANTED. NO EXPERIENCE REQUIRED.
Board and lodging, a coat, and a wage better than the quarry pays.
Nine names on the sheet under it. Six of them are quarry names.
A relief map of Caelora under glass, pins in it, and pale grey thread
run between the pins. The threads all end in the same place:
open sea, a long way off the east coast, where there is nothing to survey.
A cabinet of core samples in numbered tubes, drilled from under the city.
The numbers run to two hundred and eleven.
Nobody drills two hundred and eleven holes looking for stone.
A workbench, and on it a buoy stripped to its frame:
a float, an anchor chain, and an instrument nobody here can name
sitting where a thermometer ought to be.
A tank of clear water with a scale model of a harbour wall in it,
and a paddle that makes waves to order.
The card says the Foundation rebuilt Tideglass's sea defences for nothing.
A door at the back, plain, with a good lock on it.
The plate says STORES. The lock does not say STORES.

_plan: Everything in this room is true and everything in this room is doing good, and the player should walk out liking the Foundation. The unease is entirely in the margins -- flat coastal weather traces, two hundred core samples, threads on a map that end in open water, one very good lock on a stores cupboard -- and none of it is pointed at. Cassian is not named. Nobody is sinister. Come back after Act 4 and every one of these labels reads differently.
